description: Persist a completion time (completedAt) on the issue entity, write it on terminal transitions, backfill it for already-terminal issues from completion events, expose it through the read models, and switch the dashboard 'shipped today' / 'recently completed' surfaces from updatedAt to completedAt so post-completion edits no longer move the needle.

tasks.title: Persist completedAt on issue entity and write it on terminal transitions
tasks.description: Add a nullable `CompletedAt` field to the Issue entity (backing field + init setter, symmetric with ArchivedAt, riding inside the existing Issues.State JSON snapshot via IssueStore — no new DB column). Write it from the transition `now` in Complete (done) and Close (cancelled) in Issue.Transitions.cs; leave Reopen unchanged so the prior terminal moment survives; re-completing overwrites to the latest terminal moment. Capture `now` once per transition so completedAt and updatedAt share the same instant (mirroring the Archive idiom).
acceptanceCriteria: Issue entity exposes a nullable CompletedAt (DateTime?) persisted in the state JSON snapshot; no new database column is added.
Complete transition sets CompletedAt from the captured transition timestamp when entering done; Close sets it when entering cancelled.
Reopen does NOT clear CompletedAt (prior terminal moment retained).
Re-completing after reopen overwrites CompletedAt to the new terminal-transition moment, reflecting the most recent completion.
A non-terminal issue (backlog/in_progress) has CompletedAt == null.
Unit tests cover: in_progress->done writes the field; close->cancelled writes the field; reopen preserves the field; reopen->start->done overwrites to the latest moment; non-terminal is null.
`npm test` (server) passes under TreatWarningsAsErrors.
tasks.output: Updated packages/server Issue entity (Issue.cs), terminal transitions (Issue.Transitions.cs), and accompanying unit tests proving terminal-write + reopen/re-complete semantics.
tasks.notes: Follow design D1 (nullable field in JSON snapshot, init setter) and D2 (capture `now` once, set _completedAt then Touch). Do not stamp timestamps onto the event records themselves (rejected alternative). Domain events carry no timestamp payload by design.

tasks.title: One-time idempotent backfill migration of completedAt from IssueEvents
tasks.description: Add a raw-SQL EF Core migration under Infrastructure/Data/Migrations that backfills completedAt for issues already in a terminal state, deriving each value from the IssueEvents log: done issues take MAX(Time) of com.mohist.issue.work-completed events, cancelled issues take MAX(Time) of com.mohist.issue.closed events, keyed by Source = '/mohist/issues/' || IssueId, gated on completedAt IS NULL for idempotency. Down no-ops (field is additive).
acceptanceCriteria: A new EF migration exists under packages/server Infrastructure/Data/Migrations and runs as part of Database.MigrateAsync at startup.

Migration Up executes UPDATE...json_set for done issues (from com.mohist.issue.work-completed MAX(Time)) and cancelled issues (from com.mohist.issue.closed MAX(Time)), each WHERE completedAt IS NULL AND status matches.
Backfill is idempotent: re-running the migration does not change an already-backfilled or live-written completedAt (gated on completedAt IS NULL).
Down migration is a no-op (does not strip completedAt, preserving live-written values).

An in-memory SQLite migration spec (mirroring EpicIdleRenameMigrationSpecs) covers: a done issue backfilled from its work-completed event time; a cancelled issue backfilled from its closed event time; a second run is a no-op; an issue with an already-set completedAt is not clobbered.
`npm test` (server) passes.
tasks.output: New EF migration file under Infrastructure/Data/Migrations plus an in-memory SQLite spec proving backfill correctness and idempotency.
tasks.notes: Follow design D3 exactly, including the COALESCE status extraction (camelCase/PascalCase) and Source keying. Use IssueEvents.Time (TEXT ISO-8601) verbatim via json_set; the migration spec must round-trip a real persisted Time value through IssueStore.Deserialize to prove STJ DateTime? parses it. See Risks for the terminal-but-no-event edge case (left NULL intentionally).

tasks.title: Expose completedAt in issue list, detail, and archived-detail read models
tasks.description: Add a nullable string CompletedAt to IssueInfo and IssueReadModel, and project it in IssueQuerier.ToInfo as issue.CompletedAt?.ToString("o") (next to ArchivedAt). Because archived detail shares the identical endpoint/DTO/path with regular detail, this single projection point satisfies list, detail, and archived-detail exposure with no archived-specific code.
acceptanceCriteria: IssueInfo and IssueReadModel expose CompletedAt as a nullable ISO-8601 string.
IssueQuerier.ToInfo projects issue.CompletedAt?.ToString("o") (ToReadModel copies it through).
Issue list response includes completedAt set to the terminal-transition moment for done/cancelled issues and null for non-terminal issues.
GET /api/issues/:number detail response includes completedAt for terminal issues.
Archived-issue detail (same path/DTO) exposes completedAt identical to the non-archived detail value.
Tests cover: list includes completedAt for a done issue; detail includes completedAt for a cancelled issue; non-terminal exposes null; archived detail exposes the same completedAt as pre-archive.
`npm test` (server) passes.
tasks.output: Updated IssueInfo / IssueReadModel DTOs and IssueQuerier.ToInfo projection in packages/server, plus read-model projection tests.
tasks.notes: Per design D4 there is no separate archived-detail endpoint — adding the field to the shared projection automatically reaches both detail paths. Keep the format consistent with existing createdAt/archivedAt (ToString("o")).

tasks.title: Switch dashboard shipped-today and recently-completed to completedAt on the web
tasks.description: On the web, add completedAt?: string to the Issue entity type, then switch the factory-status shippedToday derivation to count only done issues whose completedAt falls within the current calendar day (with a null guard), and switch the Dashboard Digest recently-completed bucket to sort by completedAt desc with timestampFor reading completedAt (?? updatedAt as a display-only fallback). Leave the Digest failed bucket (updatedAt) and archived bucket (archivedAt) untouched. The ArchivedPage 'Completed' label reads completedAt ?? updatedAt.
acceptanceCriteria: Web Issue entity type (packages/web/src/entities/issue/model/issue.ts) has completedAt?: string.
factory-status shippedToday counts issues with status === 'done' && completedAt && isTodayLocal(completedAt); a null/undefined completedAt excludes the issue from the count.
A done issue completed on a prior day whose updatedAt is bumped to today (post-completion edit) is NOT counted as shipped today.
Digest recently-completed bucket sorts by completedAt desc; rows display number, title, and a relative timestamp sourced from completedAt (?? updatedAt display fallback).
Digest recently-failed bucket ordering/display remains on updatedAt; recently-archived remains on archivedAt (unchanged).
ArchivedPage 'Completed' label reads completedAt ?? updatedAt.
A done issue edited after completion does NOT jump to the top of the recently-completed list.
Tests cover: shippedToday derivation (today vs prior day, null guard, post-completion-edit no re-count); digest completed ordering by completedAt desc; archived page label fallback.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.output: Updated web Issue type, factory-status derivation (widgets/factory-status/model/), recent-digest completed bucket (entities/issue/lib/recent-digest.ts, widgets/dashboard-digest/ui/DashboardDigestWidget.tsx), ArchivedPage label (pages/archived/ui/ArchivedPage.tsx), and accompanying vitest tests.
tasks.notes: Follow design D5 strictly: completedAt is the strict sort/count key; updatedAt fallbacks are DISPLAY-ONLY safety nets that must not affect ordering or the shipped-today count (the count is gated on completedAt being present). Web changes are internally testable with mocked completedAt data even before backend availability thanks to the fallbacks.
